'''Boris Vladimirovich Struminsky''' ({{langx|ru|Борис Владимирович Струминский}}; 14 August 1939 – 18 January 2003) was a [[RSFSR|Russian]] and [[Ukraine|Ukrainian]] physicist known for his contribution to theoretical [[elementary particle physics]].

==Biography==
Boris Struminsky was born on 14 August 1939 in [[Malakhovka, Moscow Oblast|Malakhovka]], a settlement in Ukhtomsky District (now [[Lyuberetsky District]]), [[Moscow Oblast]], [[RSFSR]], [[USSR]].<ref name="itf_kiev">Борис Володимирович Струмінський (14.08.1939—18.01.2003) {{in lang|uk}}, Bogolyubov Institute for Theoretical Physics</ref> His father was [[academician]] Vladimir Vasilyevich Struminsky (1914—1998).<ref name="vestnik">{{cite web| script-title = ru:По ту сторону звукового барьера| author = С.К. Бетяев| publisher = Вестник Российской Академии наук, т.74, №12, с.1118—1122 (2004)| url = http://vivovoco.rsl.ru/VV/JOURNAL/VRAN/2004/STRUM.HTM| language = ru| accessdate = 2013-11-25| url-status = dead| archiveurl = https://web.archive.org/web/20131214123840/http://vivovoco.rsl.ru/VV/JOURNAL/VRAN/2004/STRUM.HTM| archivedate = 2013-12-14}}</ref>

After finishing the school Boris Struminsky started his studies at [[MSU Faculty of Physics|Faculty of Physics]] of [[Moscow State University]], which he graduated in 1962.<ref name="fizfak">{{cite web
 | title      = Faculty of Physics Alumni of 1962
 | website    = 
 | author     = 
 | publisher  = Faculty of Physics Alumni Union — upmsu.phys.msu.ru
 | url        = http://upmsu.phys.msu.ru/div1962.html
 | language   = ru
 | date       = 
 | accessdate = 2013-11-24
}}</ref>

From 1962 to 1965 Struminsky was a doctoral student at [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]] in Moscow. From 1965 he continued his work at the same institute as a junior researcher. In 1965 he successfully defended his doctoral ([[Candidate of Sciences|C.Sc.]]) thesis devoted to ''Higher-order symmetries and composite models of elementary particles''.<ref name="itf_kiev" />

In 1966 Struminsky started his work at [[Joint Institute for Nuclear Research]] in [[Dubna]], first as a researcher, and then, from 1967, as a senior researcher of the Laboratory of Theoretical Physics.<ref name="itf_kiev" />

In 1971 Boris Struminsky moved to Institute for Theoretical Physics of the [[Academy of Science of the Ukrainian SSR]] (now [[Bogolyubov Institute for Theoretical Physics]] of the [[National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine]]) in [[Kyiv]], where he worked until the end of his life, first as a senior researcher, and then as a leading researcher. In 1973 Struminsky successfully defended his [[Doktor nauk|D.Sc.]] thesis devoted to ''Finite energy sum rules and the dual resonance model''.<ref name="itf_kiev" />

==Research==
The main scientific results of Boris Struminsky are related to the [[quark]] structure of [[hadron]]s — [[elementary particles]] held together by the [[strong force]]. His 1965 paper<ref >{{cite arXiv
 | title  = A contribution to the history of quarks: Boris Struminsky's 1965 JINR publication
 | author = Fyodor Tkachov
 | date   = 13 December 2009
 | class  = physics.hist-ph
 | eprint = 0904.0343
 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.inr.ac.ru/~ftkachov/struminsky/ |first=B.V. |last=Struminsky |title=Magnetic moments of baryons in the quark model. JINR P-1939, Dubna |date=7 January 1965 |access-date=9 September 2025}}</ref> contained an idea to introduce a new [[quantum number]] for the quarks, which was later called a [[color charge]]. Later on, this has become one of the basic ideas of [[quantum chromodynamics]] — the theory describing strong interaction of elementary particles.<ref name="seminar">{{cite web
 | title      = On the color of quarks in Kiev
 | website    = 
 | author     = 
 | publisher  = Dubna — JINR Weekly (Еженедельник ОИЯИ), No. 20 (4160)
 | url        = http://wwwinfo.jinr.ru/~jinrmag/win/2013/20/se20.htm
 | date       = May 24, 2013
 | accessdate = 2013-11-25
}}</ref>

Many papers by Boris Struminsky deal with various problems related to the structure of hadrons, as well as interaction of hadrons and nuclei. He published about 100 papers devoted to these topics.<ref name="itf_kiev" />

==Recognition of the discovery: Sociological aspect==
In 1988 the group of scientists (A.M. Baldin, P.N. Bogolyubov, V.A. Matveev, A.N. Tavkhelidze, R.M. Muradyan) was awarded the [[Lenin Prize]] "for a cycle of works on the "New quantum number — color charge and establishment of dynamic regularities in the quark structure of elementary particles and atomic nuclei" (1965—1977)". (See: [[:ru:Лауреаты Ленинской премии#1988|Lenin Prize Laureates for 1988]])

B. V. Struminsky, who discovered a new quantum number — color charge — was not awarded the Lenin Prize "for a cycle of works on the "New quantum number — color charge..." (1965—1977)".

This situation is so striking that it requires a more detailed description in terms of the sociology of science.

* V.A. Matveev, B.V. Struminsky, and A.N. Tavkhelidze, [https://dx.doi.org/10.1016/0031-9163(66)90160-0 Dispersion sum rules and SU(3) symmetry],  ''[[Physics Letters]]'', 22, No.2, 146, 1966
